chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim or someone else, from Safwan, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said:
The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) prohibited a man from responding to another or speaking to him while he is engaged in defecation, until he has finished.

Then he said: When he finishes his need and intends to perform istibra', let him stroke with his middle finger beneath his testicles toward the base of the penis two or three times. Then he places his index finger beneath the penis and his thumb above it, and passes them along it with firm pressure from its base to the tip of the glans, once, twice, or three times, so that whatever residual urine is within it may come out.

key_terms.اَلِاسْتِبْرَاءُ: post-urination purification procedure; a required Shia jurisprudential practice to ensure complete voiding before wudu
key_terms.اَلْحَشَفَةُ: glans; the tip of the male reproductive organ
key_terms.اَلْغَائِطُ: defecation; the act of relieving the bowels (classically also the low-lying depression used for this purpose)
key_terms.اَلْمُسَبِّحَةُ: index finger (lit. 'the glorifying finger', named for its use when pointing in the shahada gesture and in tasbih)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct step-by-step method for performing istibra' after urination according to Imam al-Rida (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Safwan from Imam al-Rida (AS), transmits a prophetic prohibition against speaking to or answering others while relieving the bowels, until one finishes. The Imam then delivers precise, step-by-step instructions for istibra' — the post-urination purification procedure — specifying exact finger movements to expel residual urine, a prerequisite for valid taharah before salat in Shia fiqh.
